title: BOFT logical experts versus expert tying, gates and standard MoE
hypothesis: One shared physical linear expert plus compact task/expert butterfly Views can approximate routed specialized experts at materially lower payload bytes than untied MoE; generic gates and low-rank controls may explain any gain.
physical_object: one shared 16×16 linear expert over fixed features
controls: tied expert plus IA3 diagonal gates
tied expert plus rank-one generic residual
tied expert plus one-plane Givens view
tied expert plus four-stage BOFT view

development.allowed: validate task, router, expert training, actual serialization and routed-vs-oracle metrics

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes including router, all expert states, view codes and metadata

success_gate: At matched routed NRMSE <=0.05, BOFT logical experts use <=70% bytes of untied standard MoE and outperform the cheapest quality-matched Givens/gate/rank-one control by >=10% NRMSE.
failure_gate: BOFT fails if routed NRMSE >0.10 or simple controls match within 5%; router accuracy <0.95 invalidates routed quality inference.
amendments: Initial development exposed that the one-plane Givens view was not BOFT and that the task teacher was specifically aligned to that orbit. Added a true four-stage disjoint Givens butterfly bank and retained one-plane Givens as a simpler control before fresh access.
boundaries: Task identity is inferred by a separate shared router
No language model or natural MoE claim
Do not count logical combinations as capacity absent measured quality
